notes: Corrected one unit: the accepted alignment gave *as* to כַּ alone and marked אֲשֶׁר unrepresented under rule 22. כַּאֲשֶׁר is one Hebrew expression rendered by one English word, so rule 30 fuses the two morphemes into a single unit; rule 22 does not apply, אֲשֶׁר being neither repeated nor resumptive. The supplied copula rides with the fused prepositional predicate under rules 20 and 49, as rule 30 permits (לִפְנֵי → *was before*).

Everything else stands: partition now 30 source tokens across 27 units and 34 target tokens each used once; כְּעֵין fuses to *like unto* with its copula (rules 30, 49), and both articles on הָאוֹפַן are unrepresented because the ASV writes *a wheel* twice (rule 29).
יִהְיֶה keeps *it were*: the explicit subject הָאוֹפַן is rendered *a wheel*, so the English *it* is pleonastic and stays with the verb (rule 17).
